_doc: Where the STAND-IN's face was marked, in pixels of the crop `crop_px` of the copy named in `scan` (T-3553; the owner: "their faces must match exactly"). The `mp_<index>` marks are MediaPipe Face Landmarker's (float16 v1) points on the owner's picture, every one the correspondence table (data/humans/variation/mediapipe_hm08_landmarks.json) puts on a skin vertex, and the face's outline ring (`mpo_<index>`) on the vertices it falls on in the calibration render turned as the portrait is (`outline_yaw_deg`, the yaw of a first fit without it), at 8 px where the forehead's edge is under the hair; they were checked by eye on a 3x enlargement. The pupils are the model's iris centres; the ears were read by eye on a gridded enlargement. `prior_widen` 2 lets this many points hold the face instead of the town's average. He sits with his face turned a little to his left; his right ear shows clear of the hair, his left is hidden. Below the nose his face is under a moustache and full beard, so the points there are the model's estimate of the face beneath and carry 9 px; his menton is read by eye about 2.5 cm above the beard's lower edge (12 px), not where the beard ends. `base_body` fits against the gentleman's body's rest face.
age_note: The picture is undated and its sitter unnamed; the sitter looks about 50. The owner gave it as William L. Grey's likeness for 1904, when William was 64 (1900 census). The face is fitted as a face of 50, and the figure is drawn at that age (`likeness.drawn_age`), so the town shows the portrait's face rather than one aged 14 years past it; the person's record keeps 64.
basis: No photograph of William L. Grey is known. The owner supplied this sepia cabinet-style portrait on 2026-11-12 as the likeness to use for him in 1904 ("since we do not have photos of them you can use these likenesses"). Who sat for it and when it was made are not recorded, so it is a stand-in: his face's proportions, hair, beard and dress follow it, and none of it is evidence of how William Grey looked.
not_modelled: his own face (no photograph of him is known; this is the owner's stand-in)
the colouring (the picture is sepia; hair, beard and eye colours are readings of its tones)
the watch chain across the waistcoat (no jewellery is modelled on the town's figures)
the cut of the sack coat (the gentleman's body keeps its own frock coat, coloured as his suit)

stand_in.label: STAND-IN, NOT WILLIAM L. GREY
stand_in.card_note: No photograph of William L. Grey is known. This is a stand-in the project's owner chose as his likeness: a sepia portrait of a broad, full-bearded man with wavy hair worn long and swept back, in a dark three-piece suit with a watch chain. Its sitter is not recorded. His face, hair and dress are the model's guide; it is not William Grey.

read_by_eye.basis: Read by eye from the same picture, on axes the marks cannot measure from one three-quarter view: a broad face, a heavy jaw under the beard, a nose broad at its wings, and the eyes set under a heavy brow. These replace the gentleman's body's own lean as the prior on those axes; the marks still move them where they can. His cheeks and jowls are fitted with his side view instead (fit_views).

card._doc: What the person's card shows (T-3413, T-3478): `portrait` is cut from the copy at `portrait_from_scan_px` and scaled to `size_px` by tools/cut_portrait.py (a stand-in's label burned on it); `model` is tools/portrait_still.mjs's render of the fitted face on `body`, turned to the fit's yaw, dressed as humans.js dresses the person in town.

likeness.hair_tone_basis: Re-read from the owner's turnaround sheet of the stand-in (2026-11-13), which is in colour: his hair a mid-to-dark brown with grey through it and a grey streak at the temple, drawn a brown going grey; his beard and moustache a grizzled russet, warmest at the moustache and greyest at the chin; his eyes a light blue-grey. Colours of a stand-in, not a record.

dress.worn: dark brown three-piece suit, as the stand-in portrait

likeness._doc: What the figure takes from the stand-in, for tools/prairie_people.py: hair cut, facial hair and their colour (human-hair-styles.js), complexion, and the suit's colour on the gentleman's body (coat, waistcoat and trousers of one cloth, as the portrait's three-piece suit). Reconstructed readings of a sepia picture.

build.basis: Read by eye from the stand-in portrait (owner, 2026-11-12: "their build match is important"): a big, heavy-set man, broad through the shoulders and chest, the waistcoat full over a stomach, a thick neck in a wide collar. Axis values are a reading of a seated three-quarter portrait, not a measurement.

drawn_age.basis: Drawn at the age the stand-in portrait shows (about 50), not him recorded age of 64 in 1904, so the face matches the picture the owner chose ("their faces must match exactly"). A reading by eye of an undated picture; the record's age is unchanged.

axes_note: chin_prominence, prognathism and nose_depth move the face toward or away from a camera that looks at it nearly square, so one near-frontal picture does not measure them; they are read here from the side view in `fit_views` (T-3553, 2026-11-13).

trace.basis: The per-vertex trace (tools/trace_portrait_face.py) is withdrawn (owner, 2026-11-13: "he looks like a caveman, totally squashed nose and no nose brim", "he has no chin and almost no nose"): spot moves on the nose alone, over a face fitted from the front, could not bring the bridge and the chin with it. His side view (`profile`, the owner's turnaround sheet, from the brow to under the nose; the beard hides the rest) is now fitted together with the portrait (`fit_views`), so the nose's bridge and how far it stands out, and the chin under the beard, come from one smooth face.

profile.view: the bottom-left head, his right side (facing the viewer's right), turned about 80 degrees
profile._doc: Sheet pixels. silhouette_px: the face's line against the sheet's white ground, from the forehead to the neck, every second pixel of its outline; marks_px: MediaPipe Face Landmarker points on the side view (the visible eye's corners and lids, the lips' meeting); tragus_px read by eye, with the skin vertex the render draws there (tragus_kit_vertex) (tools/trace_portrait_profile.py).

fit_views._doc: T-3553: the axes are fitted to these pictures of the same stand-in at once, each with its own camera (tools/fit_portrait_face.py fit_views): `fronts`, MediaPipe Face Landmarker points (478, sheet pixels) on another front picture; `profile`, the side view of trace.profile (its visible eye's outer corner and lids and the lips' meeting place a side camera turned near render_yaw_deg, its nod free; its silhouette is matched by the face's own outline from that side, from the brow down `to` the neck or, under a beard, to just below the nose; `lips: height` keeps only the lips' height where a moustache hangs in front of them; `camera_sigma_deg` holds the side camera near the turn read by eye, not tipped). `extended_limits` lets an axis pass MakeHuman's +-1 where the side view asks for more.
